text: Harbour City opened the match strongly with patient, possession-based build-up involving 17 passes over 57 seconds to create a high xG chance (0.994) finished by Elias Okafor, reflecting their 4-2-3-1 formation and short passing style under Tomasz Rhee [#904] [#905]. Despite this, Seabrook Town dominated overall with 53.4% possession, 22 shots, and 3.87 xG, exploiting wide crossing play inherent in their 3-4-3 formation coach Mara Lindholm favors. Their tactical adjustment at 65', increasing press intensity (ppda drop from 6.7 to 5.8), directness (from 0.42 to 0.57), and line height, shifted their approach to an aggressive, high-line press that generated more big chances and goals [#1361]. Kian Romano’s quick counter-attacking goals in stoppage time sprung from rapid regains and minimal passes (7.2s, 2 passes), a clear product of this pressing trigger and transition mechanism [#1881] [#1882]. Marek Barros’s involvement (goal, 2 assists, 9 interceptions, and 5 key passes) underpinned Harbour City's resilience but was insufficient against Seabrook's effective overload and aggressive transition play.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for analyst audience in en

- Harbour City started strong with goals at 45' (xg 0.994) and 47' (xg 0.185) but lost 2-4 to Seabrook Town [#905,975].
- Seabrook Town scored four times including two late goals by Kian Romano (90+2' xg 0.745 and 90+3' xg 0.956) to complete the comeback [#1882,1906].
- Seabrook Town dominated possession (53.4%), shots (22 vs 10) and xG (3.87 vs 1.82) showing superior attacking play [team_stats].
- Tactical change at 65' for Seabrook Town to press higher and play more direct improved chances and contributed to the comeback [#1361].
- Marek Barros was player of the match with 1 goal, 2 assists, 5 key passes, 9 interceptions, and a 10.0 rating [player_of_the_match].

- Seabrook Town’s late goals, especially the 90+2' counter goal by Kian Romano, came from quickly regaining possession and exploiting space with just a few passes over a short time (7.2s, 2 passes) starting from a regain, indicating effective counter-attacking play that suits their higher pressing and directness setting adopted after 65' to chase the game [#1881,#1882,#1361].
- Harbour City took the lead with patient, possession-based build-up involving many short passes (17 passes over 56.9s) culminating in a high xG chance finished by Elias Okafor, reflecting their 4-2-3-1 formation and “patient short passing” style under coach Tomasz Rhee [#904,#905].
- Seabrook Town’s style emphasizes wide, crossing play from their 3-4-3, seen in Marek Barros’s goal for Harbour City from a corner cross, showing how set pieces were critical and exploited by opposition’s wing play and defensive organization [#973,#975].
- The tactical shift by Seabrook Town after 65' included a higher press and increased directness, reducing their possession but increasing pressure (ppda dropped from 6.7 to 5.8), which led to more big chances and goals, showing a switch from possession control to an aggressive, higher line approach matching their 3-4-3 wide attacking setup [#1361].
